diagnostic_evidence.quote: it is easy to know that $[\![\Pi_{h}\mathbf{v}]\!]=0$, $\forall F\in \mathcal{E}_{h}^{i}$, and together with $\Pi_{h}\mathbf{v}\cdot \mathbf{n}=0$ on $\partial\Omega$

issues.failure_explanation: The DG norm $\|\cdot\|_h$ contains the full tensor-jump penalty $\sum_F\frac{\gamma}{h_F}\|[\![\underline{\cdot}]\!]\|_{0,F}^2$, which controls tangential traces. The $H(div)$-conforming projection $\Pi_h$ has only continuous normal traces (by (s2.29)), so the full jump $[\![\underline{\Pi_h\mathbf{v}}]\!]=\Pi_h\mathbf{v}^+\otimes\mathbf{n}^++\Pi_h\mathbf{v}^-\otimes\mathbf{n}^-$ is generically nonzero and not small; only the normal jump vanishes. Hence the bound (s2.35) used in the inf-sup proof (lem2-3) and the estimate (s2.31), invoked from Nedelec's Proposition 1 for the a priori velocity error in th2-4, are false as stated for the full-jump norm and are not consequences of the cited $H(div)$ interpolation estimates. Both proofs are therefore invalid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the $H(div)$-conforming projection $\Pi_h$ by the continuous Lagrange interpolant $I_h$ in the proofs of lem2-3 and th2-4: $I_h$ satisfies the same commuting identity $\nabla\cdot I_h\mathbf{v}=\vartheta_h\nabla\cdot\mathbf{v}$ and the orthogonality $\mathbb{B}_h(I_h\mathbf{u}^f-\mathbf{u}^f,q_h)=0$, its jumps vanish on interior faces and it vanishes on $\partial\Omega$, and $\|I_h\mathbf{v}\|_h\lesssim\|\mathbf{v}\|_1$, $\|\mathbf{u}-I_h\mathbf{u}\|_h\lesssim h^s\|\mathbf{u}\|_{1+s}$ hold. Both proofs then go through with the same structure and all estimates and rates are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete inf-sup condition (lem2-3) and the optimal a priori error estimates for the source problems (th2-4) lose their proofs; the $L^2$ error estimate (th2-5) and the spectral approximation theorem (th2-7), including the gap estimate and the eigenpair error rates, lose their basis. The a posteriori section (th3-1 through th3-8) does not depend on these results.
issues.title: False full-jump DG-norm bounds for the H(div) projection invalidate the inf-sup and a priori error proofs
issues.why_classification: The two central a priori proofs are genuinely invalid as written and must be reworked, which is more than a typo-level fix; however the replacement of $\Pi_h$ by $I_h$ is a contained modification using only standard interpolation properties, preserves every result and rate, and requires no new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of (s2.88) bounds $|((\mathbb{T}-\mathbb{T}_h)\mathbf{u}_j,\mathbb{T}^*\mathbf{u}_i^*-I_h\mathbb{T}^*\mathbf{u}_i^*)|$ through the $h^r$-weighted continuity estimate (s2.16) with the regularity exponent $r\in(1/2,1]$ from (s2.25). For the interpolation error $\mathbb{T}\mathbf{u}_j-I_h\mathbb{T}\mathbf{u}_j$, (s2.65) gives $h_\tau^r|\nabla(\mathbb{T}\mathbf{u}_j-I_h\mathbb{T}\mathbf{u}_j)|_{r,\tau}\lesssim h_\tau^r|\mathbb{T}\mathbf{u}_j|_{1,\tau}$ when $s<1$ and $\lesssim h_\tau^{r+s-1}$ when $s\ge1$, so (s2.88) is $\lesssim h^{2r}$ for $s\in[r,1]$ and $\lesssim h^{2s-1}$ for $s>1$, not the claimed $h^{2s}$. The rate $h^{2s}$ in the range $s\in(r,1]$ is recovered only by choosing the weight in (s2.16) equal to $s$ (legitimate since $s\le1$); for $s\in(1,k]$ the argument delivers at most $h^{2s-1}$. Thus the advertised rate in the high-regularity regime — the $h^{2k}$ behavior the numerics report for $k=2,3$ — is unsupported by the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict th2-7 to $s\le1$ — the range furnished by the assumed regularity (s2.25) — and apply (s2.16) with weight $r=s$, which yields $h^{2s}$; alternatively restate (s2.80) with the rate $h^{r+s}$ (respectively $h^{2s-1}$ for $s>1$) that the argument actually proves.
issues.overall_effect: The cluster eigenvalue estimate (s2.80) of th2-7 is proven only at rate $h^{2r}$ as written (or $h^{2s}$ for $s\le1$ with the weight taken as $s$); for $s\in(1,k]$ the claimed $h^{2s}$ rate has no proof, so the theorem's advertised rate in the high-regularity regime, including the $h^{2k}$ convergence observed numerically, is not supported.
issues.title: Theorem th2-7: the cluster eigenvalue rate h^{2s} is not established for s>1 (nor for s>r as written)
issues.why_classification: The rate claim is materially stronger than what the proof delivers exactly in the advertised high-regularity regime $s\in(1,k]$; the supported repair is a contained hypothesis restriction to $s\le1$, consistent with the paper's own regularity assumption, so the main a priori results survive and no new architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Solve Eqs.(\ref{s2.8})-(\ref{s2.9}) and (\ref{s4.4})-(\ref{s4.5}) on $\mathcal{T}_{h_{l}}$ for the discrete solution

issues.failure_explanation: On $\mathbb{X}_h\times\mathbb{X}_h$ the viscous consistency terms and the convection terms of $\mathbb{A}_h$ and $\widehat{\mathbb{A}}_h$ do coincide by Green's formula, but the interior penalty parameters differ: $\mathbb{A}_h$ ((s2.10)) uses $\gamma/h_F$ while $\widehat{\mathbb{A}}_h$ ((s4.6)) uses $\mu\gamma/h_F$. Their difference restricted to $\mathbb{X}_h\times\mathbb{X}_h$ is $(1-\mu)\sum_F\int_F\frac{\gamma}{h_F}[\![\underline{\mathbf{u}}]\!]:\overline{[\![\underline{\mathbf{v}}]\!]}$, which is nonzero for $\mu\neq1$. Hence the adjoint eigenproblem actually solved in Algorithm 1, (s4.4)-(s4.5), is not the adjoint problem (s2.48)-(s2.49) on which the a posteriori theory and the estimator $\eta^*_h$ are built, and the equivalence claim is false as stated (it holds only for $\mu=1$, the case of all reported experiments).

failure_location.quote: We deduce by Green's formula that \begin{align} &~~~\mathbb{A}_{h}(\mathbf{v}_{h},\mathbf{u}^{*}_{h})-\widehat{\mathbb{A}}_{h}(\mathbf{v}_{h},\mathbf{u}^{*}_{h})=0,~~~\forall \mathbf{v}_{h},\mathbf{u}^{*}_{h}\in \mathbb{X}_{h}. \end{align} Hence, the adjoint problem (\ref{s4.4})-(\ref{s4.5}) is equivalent to the adjoint problem (\ref{s2.48})-(\ref{s2.49}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the spurious factor $\mu$ from the penalty in $\widehat{\mathbb{A}}_h$ (s4.6) — or equivalently use $\mu\gamma/h_F$ in the primal penalty (s2.10); the two forms then agree on $\mathbb{X}_h\times\mathbb{X}_h$ for all $\mu$ and the equivalence claim holds.
issues.overall_effect: For $\mu\neq1$ the adjoint eigenpairs $(\lambda^*_{j,h},\mathbf{u}^*_{j,h},p^*_{j,h})$ entering the adaptive loop of Algorithm 1 are solutions of a different discrete adjoint problem than the one treated by the reliability/effectiveness theory, so the adjoint error control described in the paper does not apply to the computed adjoint quantities. All numerical experiments use $\mu=1$, where the two formulations coincide.
issues.title: Claimed equivalence of the two discrete adjoint eigenproblems is false for mu != 1 (penalty parameter mismatch)
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction to the penalty parameter restores the claimed equivalence, and all reported experiments use $\mu=1$ where the claim already holds, so no result, rate, or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The face flux jump in $\eta_{F_\tau}$ contains $[\![\mathbf{u}_h\otimes\beta]\!]=[\![\mathbf{u}_h]\!]\beta$ (since $[\![\mathbf{u}]\!]=0$), i.e., the jump of the discrete velocity, which is not controlled by $\|\nabla(\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{u}_h)\|_{0,\omega(\tau)}+\|p-p_h\|_{0,\omega(\tau)}$. In the bubble-function argument the face convection term $\int_F[\![\mathbf{u}_h]\!]\beta\cdot\overline{\Theta}$ either contributes the unscaled jump $\|[\![\mathbf{u}_h]\!]\|_{0,F}$ or, after integration by parts against the bubble $\Theta$, the $L^2$ error $\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{u}_h\|_{0,\omega(\tau)}$; neither appears in the stated right-hand side of (s3.25) (or of the adjoint (s3.28)). The local face efficiency bound is therefore false as stated and the global effectiveness estimate th3-6 is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing contribution to (s3.25)/(s3.28): $\eta_{F_\tau}\lesssim\|\nabla(\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{u}_h)\|_{0,\omega(\tau)}+\|p-p_h\|_{0,\omega(\tau)}+\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{u}_h\|_{0,\omega(\tau)}+(\sum_{\tau\in\omega(\tau)}h_\tau^2\|\lambda\mathbf{u}-\lambda_h\mathbf{u}_h\|_{0,\tau}^2)^{1/2}$ (the discrete jump being absorbable into $\eta_{J_\tau}$). Since $\|\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{u}_h\|_{0,\omega(\tau)}\lesssim h_\tau^r(|||\mathbf{u}-\mathbf{u}_h||| +\|p-p_h\|_0)$ by (s2.76), th3-6 and the corollary are recovered with unchanged conclusions.
issues.overall_effect: The local face efficiency bound (s3.25)/(s3.28) is false as stated, so the global effectiveness estimate (th3-6) and the cluster equivalence claimed in cor:added-1 are not established; the paper's advertised effectiveness of the estimator for approximate eigenfunctions is unsupported in its current form.
issues.title: Lemma lem3-5: the local face efficiency bound (s3.25) omits the convection-jump contribution and is false as stated
issues.why_classification: The advertised effectiveness of the estimator rests on a local bound that omits a genuine contribution of the convection part of the face flux jump; repairing it requires redoing the face bubble estimate with an additional (higher-order) term, but the final global effectiveness and the cluster equivalence survive, so the loss is limited and no new global architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of (s2.78) requires $|(\mathbf{u}_h,\mathbf{v}_h)|\ge c>0$ uniformly in $h$, which follows from $|(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{u}^*)|>0$. For a defective eigenvalue, individual eigenfunctions in the cluster can satisfy $(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{u}^*)=0$ (Jordan-chain orthogonality), so the lower bound fails and (s2.78) is unproven. th3-8 invokes (s2.78) with $[\mathbf{v}_h,q_h]=[\mathbf{u}_h^*,p_h^*]$ under only 'the conditions of Theorem th3-1', which do not exclude defective eigenvalues; hence the eigenvalue estimator bound (s3.33) is not established for defective eigenvalues. The paper's own corollary already imposes the non-defective restriction, showing the hypothesis is needed.

failure_location.quote: Under the conditions of Theorem \ref{th3-1}, there holds

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the eigenvalue is non-defective to th3-8 and lem3-7, matching the restriction already used in cor:added-1; then $|(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{u}^*)|>0$ yields the required uniform lower bound and the proof goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The a posteriori eigenvalue estimator bound (s3.33) is asserted for all eigenvalues but the proof covers only the non-defective case; for defective eigenvalues the duality pairing can vanish and the bound is unproven, so the advertised reliability of the eigenvalue estimator does not extend to defective eigenvalues as stated.
issues.title: Theorem th3-8 (and Lemma lem3-7) lack the non-defective hypothesis needed for the uniform lower bound on the eigenfunction pairing
issues.why_classification: The eigenvalue estimator bound is stated for all eigenvalues but the proof needs a non-defective hypothesis; adding it (as the paper's corollary already does) is a local repair that preserves the result for simple and semi-simple eigenvalues but withdraws the defective case, a limited scope reduction rather than a new proof architecture.
